title: Sampling Machine
summary: Draw random crews from the Crew Log and watch their averages form a bell, even from badly skewed data. Then simulate it with sample() and replicate().
hints: `sample(hours, size = 30, replace = TRUE)` draws one crew of 30 missions.
`replicate(1000, mean(sample(hours, size = 30, replace = TRUE)))` repeats that 1,000 times and keeps each crew's mean.
The simulated SE is the SD of the means, `sd(crew_means)`; the formula is `sd(hours) / sqrt(30)`. Then `hist(crew_means)`.

goals.text: Draw at least **500 crews of n = 2** and look at the pile of crew averages.
goals.detail: Still lopsided: averages of two skewed values are skewed too. Compare the skew reading with the population's.

goals.text: Raise the crew size to **n = 30 or more** and draw at least **1,000 crews**.
goals.detail: The hours are badly skewed, yet the crew averages pile up into a bell around μ. That's the Central Limit Theorem at work.

goals.text: Get the **standard error under 200 hours**, with at least 500 crews drawn.
goals.detail: The SE is the SD of the crew averages, and it shrinks with √n: to halve it you need four times the crew.
